But I also think that software patents are completely ludicrous. There are many reasons for this but I think the most simple and pragmatic is because people invent things simultaneously with a very high regularity. For instance back in the early 2000 period there was a shadow algorithm, primarily for use in games, that a number of people invented about the same time period. However, one of these people successfully patented it and started trying to extort cash from everybody else. Note there had even been a talk given prior to the patent application discussing the technique by another developer. I have no idea what constitutes "prior art" but apparently describing a technique in detail at a public event doesn't... In a further bit of irony, the technique I'm referring to is known as "Carmack's Reverse." Carmack is not the patent holder is one of the developers that ended up getting bullied by the patent holder.

On the other hand this algorithm seems to blur the line between invention and algorithm - the former where I think patents are acceptable. And it seems that the team at No Man's Sky could not figure out how to do something and so overtly used this individual's code. Hmmm...
